finding.claim: HIGH: GET /rss passes the user-supplied `u` query parameter straight to URI.open (open-uri), and returns the first 400 bytes of the response. The attacker controls the full URL (scheme, host, port, path). Because the response is returned, this is full-read SSRF. It can reach loopback, RFC-1918 services and cloud metadata such as http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/. open-uri also follows redirects, so an external URL can redirect to an internal one. Redirect risk: yes. Fix: parse the URL, check scheme and `.host` against a strict allowlist before the call, and re-validate after redirects (or disable them).
finding.source: params[:u] — HTTP query parameter `u` on GET /rss (public Sinatra route, no authentication)

trace.note: get "/rss" route handler; public ingress with no auth
params[:u] passed directly as the argument to URI.open, with no intermediate transformation
response body (first 400 bytes) returned to the caller, so the SSRF is non-blind

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, scheme check or host check exists between source and sink. TRUSTED at app.rb:5 is not referenced in this route. No authentication or middleware is present. open-uri follows redirects, so an 'only external hosts' argument does not close it.

verdict.reason: app.rb:8 passes params[:u] directly to URI.open(...).read and app.rb:9 returns the first 400 bytes, with no host or scheme check (the TRUSTED allowlist at app.rb:5 is only used in the separate /trusted route at app.rb:14), so this is non-blind SSRF.
